subject: Greenfield Health — phased private deployment: consumption, burst credits & residency

Cc: procurement@greenfieldhealth.com

Subject: Initial commercial ask — phased on-prem rollout and burst credits

Hi Marissa / Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge) but have two commercial constraints we need to resolve before we can get an internal sign-off:

1) Phased consumption model — we need to start with a pilot (3 months) on a metered consumption basis and then convert to a reserved commit if performance and cost targets are met.
2) Burst credits — our clinical workloads spike during end-of-month reporting windows. We need a way to cover short-term bursts without paying full committed capacity during the pilot.

Can Redwood propose a simple construct that lets us: a) run a 3-month metered pilot with a defined conversion path, b) get an allocation of burst tokens/credits usable during the pilot, and c) have clear billing and SOW terms for an on-prem component?

Also, our legal team will ask about data residency controls (log partitioning and KMS) and a limited SOC2 addendum. I can loop in Maya (legal) once we have a commercial sketch.

Thanks,
Evan

Hi Evan — great to hear. High-level we can do what you describe. Proposed commercial sketch below (we'll formalize after you confirm):

- Pilot (3 months): metered billing at published host rates for private deployments; capped monthly spend (stop-loss) to provide budget certainty.
- Conversion: if you convert to a 12-month reserved commitment within 30 days of pilot end, we apply a one-time conversion credit equal to 15% of pilot billed consumption (applied to the first invoice).
- Burst credits: we'll issue a pool of "burst credits" (token-based) equal to 25% of the pilot's expected monthly token consumption. Credits apply automatically during spikes and roll off at pilot end if unused.
- On-prem SOW: separate SOW for install and runbook; standard implementation fee estimate included in attachments.
- Data residency/KMS: VPC control plane + customer-managed KMS; we can add a short addendum for log partitioning. SOC2 attestation — we can provide evidence and a limited addendum for on-prem data handling.

I'll have Rafael add a short term-sheet and SOW draft and send over by EOD tomorrow. Would you like legal copied now (Maya)?

Best,

Evan — attaching a short term-sheet (PDF) and a draft SOW (DOCX) that reflect Marissa's sketch. Highlights and clarifications: 

- Pilot cap: we propose a monthly stop-loss equal to 110% of the estimated pilot spend to give Greenfield budget certainty while retaining metered economics.
- Conversion credit: 15% credit applied to first committed invoice if conversion to 12-month reserved occurs within 30 days.
- Burst credits: operationalized as token credits redeemable only for compute (not for storage or licensing). They auto-apply when a usage spike exceeds baseline. Unused credits expire at pilot end; partial refunds not available.
- Implementation fees: one-time install + site validation; can be amortized into the first 3 invoices if you prefer.
- Security addenda: proposed wordings for KMS and log partitioning are in the term-sheet appendix. SOC2 evidence will be uploaded to your secure artifact link.

If that looks okay, we'll send an updated DocuSign route with SOW and term-sheet and include your legal contact.

Marissa / Rafael — thanks for the quick turn. A few redlines from legal (high level):

1) Conversion credit: we need the conversion credit to be transferable to an affiliated entity (we run pilots centrally and sometimes assign committed contracts to an affiliate).
2) Burst credits: request to allow carrying up to 50% of unused burst credits into the first 30 days after pilot conversion if we commit.
3) Data residency: require a contractual guarantee that audit logs referencing customer PII will remain in-region; we need KMS key custody language to be explicit that keys never leave our control.
4) Indemnity & liability cap: we asked procurement to propose a modest increase to the liability cap during pilot-to-commit window (to cover initial integration risk).

Can Redwood confirm which of these are negotiable and deliver a version with the requested language so we can circulate internally?

Regards,
Maya Cohen
Senior Counsel — Greenfield Health

Subject: Re: Initial commercial ask — negotiated positions and next steps

Maya / Evan — thanks for the clear redlines. Quick responses and proposed compromise positions below so we can move to DocuSign: 

1) Conversion credit transferability: acceptable with a short assignment clause and verification that the assignee is an affiliate; we'll add an assignment representation and notify Redwood billing.

2) Burst credits carry-forward: we can allow carry-forward of up to 30% of unused burst credits into the first 30 days after conversion (not 50%). Rationale: burst credits are priced below committed unit economics; a limited carry-forward balances risk.

3) Data residency / KMS: we will add explicit custody language: customer-managed KMS for key material in the on-prem components; control-plane logs that contain PII will be retained in-region only and accessible via your audit export. We will propose specific SLA language in the addendum.

4) Liability cap during pilot: we can temporarily increase the liability cap for pilot-related integration claims to 2x the pilot fees (limited to integration failures only). This is a carveout, not a general increase.

Next steps: if you accept these positions, we'll produce a redlined term-sheet and updated SOW and route for signature. We can also schedule a 30-minute legal call to finalize wording.

Marissa / Rafael — please confirm if you want the DocuSign envelope to include the amended addendum or to send the term-sheet and SOW first for internal review.

Thanks,
